title: Lesson 4: BLESS - Serve with Loving Sacrifice
description: Praying, listening, and eating have built the bridge. Now it is time to care with action for someone else's good. Jesus came not to be served but to serve, and He calls His followers into the same posture. This lesson shows you how to serve from freedom rather than for approval, with the time, talents, and treasure you already have.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you learned to listen well and to open your table. Now comes the most active of the five rhythms. Serving is where you stop being only present and start to sacrifice for someone else. Before any of it begins, Jesus has something to show you. Not a sermon, but a scene.

blocks.alt: Jesus kneeling with a basin and a towel, washing the feet of His disciples at the Last Supper

blocks.title: The Towel and the Basin
blocks.text:
It was the night before the cross. Jesus and His disciples sat down for the Passover meal. Jesus knew exactly what was coming: Judas about to betray Him, Peter about to deny Him, the rest about to scatter. He had every reason to ask for comfort or to talk about His death.

Instead, He stood up from the table, took off His outer robe, wrapped a towel around His waist, poured water into a basin, and began to wash His disciples' feet. The Lord became the slave. The teacher took the lowest job in the house.

"Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going back to God, rose from supper. He laid aside his outer garments, and taking a towel, tied it around his waist. Then he poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples' feet." (John 13:3-5)

Peter could not stand it. "You shall never wash my feet." Jesus answered, "If I do not wash you, you have no part with me." Then He sat back down and gave them the line they would never forget. "If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet." (John 13:14)

Jesus had every right to be served, but He chose to serve. He had hours left to live, and He spent them washing dirty feet. That is the picture He wanted His followers to keep: not power, not status, but a towel and a basin.
Greatness, Upside Down
A few days earlier, the mother of James and John had asked Jesus to seat her sons at His right and left in His kingdom. The other ten heard and got angry. Jesus called them all together.

You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them. It shall not be so among you. But whoever would be great among you must be your servant, and whoever would be first among you must be your slave, even as the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.

The world measures greatness by how many people serve you. Jesus measures it by how many people you serve. The world counts followers; Jesus counts feet washed. The world says climb; Jesus says kneel. In His kingdom the way down is the way up.
4.1 - Where are you most tempted to measure greatness the way the world does?
Serve from Freedom

This is where many Christians get stuck. They hear serve others and feel one more requirement, one more thing they have to do. The gospel does something with serving that nothing else does. It frees you to serve without earning anything by it.
For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another.

Paul does not say serve to earn your acceptance with God. He says you have already been called to freedom, and love flows out of that freedom toward your neighbor. Your debt is paid. Your standing is settled. You have nothing left to prove, so you can wash someone's feet without needing them to wash yours back.

Here is a picture worth holding onto. God is not a watering bucket you have to keep filling. God is a mountain spring, always flowing, always overflowing. You do not honor a spring by hauling buckets up the path and pouring them in. You honor it by kneeling, drinking, and being filled until you overflow into others. You drink from Jesus, He fills you, and the people around you get the overflow. John Piper says, "Love is the overflow of joy in God that gladly meets the needs of others."
Whoever serves, as one who serves by the strength that God supplies, in order that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ. To him belong glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen.
The strength comes from God, the serving is yours, and the glory goes back to Him. You do not serve to fill God up. You serve because He keeps filling you.
4.2 - What would it feel like if every act of service this week came from the overflow of joy in the God who has already served you?
Time, Talents, and Treasure
Serving is the everyday way you pour out three things God has put in your hands. Carry them as three words: time, talents, and treasure.

blocks.title: Time, Talents, and Treasure
content: Time. Hours given to people who can never pay you back: an afternoon helping someone move, a ride to the doctor, an unhurried talk on the porch.
Talents. The skills God built into you, used for someone outside your circle: fixing a car, tutoring a student, cooking a meal, untangling a form.
Treasure. Your money, your home, your tools, and your stuff: a small bill paid quietly, a borrowed truck, a spare room for a hard season.

blocks.text: Serving means letting any one of the three be inconvenienced for someone else's need. None of it was ever yours to clutch; all of it was given to you to give. You have been praying for your people, listening to them, and eating with them. Now you get to make their life a little lighter, in a way they can see and touch.
4.3 - Of your time, talents, and treasure, which is your biggest growth area, and what is one way you could develop it?
This Week's Practice

Choose one specific way to serve someone on your prayer card this week with your time, your talents, or your treasure. Keep it simple: drop off a meal, watch their kids for an hour, help with the yard, or quietly cover a small bill. Do it without expecting anything back. Then ask the Spirit to fill you up again. That is the rhythm: drink, overflow, drink again. Service that starts as duty runs dry by Tuesday. Service that starts as joy in Jesus lasts a lifetime.
4.4 - How would you explain to a friend why you serve without needing anything back?
Lesson 4 Review

Jesus came not to be served but to serve, and on His last night the King knelt with a towel and a basin. Greatness in His kingdom is measured by whose feet you wash, not by who washes yours. You serve from freedom, because your acceptance with God is already settled. You drink from the spring and overflow instead of hauling buckets to fill Him up. And you give your time, talents, and treasure to people who could never pay you back.
In the next lesson, you will learn the last rhythm, Story: how to share your own story and the story of Jesus with the people you have been blessing.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?

The BLESS rhythms are adapted from BLESS: 5 Everyday Ways to Love Your Neighbor and Change the World by Dave Ferguson and Jon Ferguson. The mountain spring picture and the quoted line about love come from Desiring God by John Piper.
